query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: open_neg_tech_signals
per_column.rationale: Count of negative technology-related mentions in the open response; a genuine content feature derived from text, not from the satisfaction score, that plausibly correlates with low satisfaction.

per_column.name: open_neg_engagement_signals
per_column.rationale: Negative engagement mentions extracted from free text; an independent signal outside the focus that can carry predictive value.

per_column.name: open_neg_social_signals
per_column.rationale: Negative social-aspect mentions; a legitimate text-derived predictor distinct from the satisfaction rating.

per_column.name: open_neg_comprehension_signals
per_column.rationale: Negative comprehension mentions; a substantive content feature plausibly linked to satisfaction.

per_column.name: open_neg_teacher_signals
per_column.rationale: Negative teacher-related mentions; independent thematic signal usable as a predictor.

per_column.name: open_neg_emotional_signals
per_column.rationale: Negative emotional expressions in text; a plausible predictor of satisfaction that is not a restatement of the score.

per_column.name: open_pos_signals
per_column.rationale: Count of positive mentions; carries predictive signal about satisfaction and lies outside the focus variable.

per_column.name: open_neg_categories_hit
per_column.rationale: Number of distinct negative themes triggered; a breadth-of-negativity feature derived from text, legitimately predictive.

per_column.name: open_net_neg_per100words
per_column.rationale: Density-normalized net negativity from the open response; a text-derived continuous feature, not a function of the satisfaction score.

per_column.name: open_predicts_low_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: A binary flag whose very name/purpose is a direct prediction/proxy of the low-satisfaction outcome. It is essentially a restatement of the target label and would leak the focus rather than serve as an independent predictor.

judge.rationale: Nearly all added columns are thematically structured negative/positive signal counts and a normalized negativity density extracted from the open_response text. These lie outside the satisfaction rating and plausibly carry real predictive signal, making them legitimate features. The set has good coverage across distinct themes (tech, engagement, social, comprehension, teacher, emotional) plus positive tone and breadth, giving substantive predictive leverage beyond the original columns. The lone failure is open_predicts_low_satisfaction, which is a target-proxy label (leakage/restatement of the outcome) and must not be used as a feature. Excluding that column, the feature set is strong; utility is capped short of maximal because the individual signal columns are sparse (heavily zero) and somewhat redundant with one another.
